subject: Clarify: Non-training assurance + retention for logs, backups, and debug artifacts
messages:
From: Alice Zhang <alice@fintechco.com>

Cc: FintechCo Security <security@fintechco.com>, Bob Lee <bob.legal@fintechco.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick confirm: Do you train on customer data? + logs/backups question

Hannah —

We're finalizing risk review for our Redwood pilot and have two tight asks from legal/security: 1) a plain-language confirmation that Redwood does not use our customer content to train models; 2) a short description of retention windows and exceptions for logs, backups, and any developer debug snapshots.

Specifically: 
- Are any customer request/response pairs or telemetry ever included in training datasets (even aggregated)?
- What retention windows apply to: request logs, debugging snapshots, KV caches, periodic backups, and archived snapshots?
- Any scenarios where backups/snapshots are kept longer (e.g., for legal hold, incident response)?

Appreciate a succinct reply; we may need a tech attestation PDF for procurement.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Zhang
Head of Security Engineering, FintechCo

Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 07 Jul 2025 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick confirm: Do you train on customer data? + logs/backups question

Hi Alice —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answer up front: Redwood does not train or fine-tune our model weights on customer-provided content from hosted or dedicated deployments as part of our standard operating procedures. I'll have Mina and Marcus add definitive retention windows and call out the narrow exceptions.

High-level points to note:
- No-training guarantee: We separate product telemetry from training pipelines by default; customer message content is NOT routed into model training datasets.
- Telemetry vs. content: We collect service telemetry (errors, performance metrics) for service health. This telemetry is aggregated and stripped of PII before any ML research use.
- Short-term operational artifacts: Request logs, ephemeral KV cache, and debug snapshots may exist for troubleshooting; they have defined TTLs.

Action: Mina, Marcus — can you provide the specific windows (and the mechanism for legal hold or export) and attach the SOC2 summary and a simple diagram for Alice? Alice — happy to produce a one-page attestation once we confirm the windows.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Security & Privacy Operations
Redwood Inference

Hi Alice — hi Hannah —

Below are the concrete retention policies and operational notes. I kept it pragmatic so you can paste into your procurement questionnaire.

1) Model training and customer content
- Commitment: Redwood does not use customer request/response content to train or improve the weights of any production models. This applies to Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private (unless customer explicitly opts in via a written data-sharing agreement).
- Aggregated telemetry: Service-level telemetry (e.g., token throughput, error rates) may be retained in aggregated, non-reversible form for research. No raw customer text is included.

2) Retention windows (default)
- Request logs (indexing metadata such as timestamps, route, latency): 30 days. PII-sensitive fields are redacted where applicable.
- Full request/response payloads (where stored for debugging): 7 days by default. These are stored encrypted and access-controlled; deletion is automated after TTL.
- KV cache and ephemeral model caches: Evicted within 24 hours for typical workloads; per-customer cache TTL configurable in Dedicated/private deployments.
- Debug snapshots (for reproducing incidents): 90 days for incidents that require root-cause analysis; otherwise not retained beyond 7 days. Snapshots are tagged and access-limited.
- Periodic backups and archived snapshots: Backups retained for 90 days by default. Archived snapshots for compliance/legal holds can be retained longer but require a documented legal hold process and customer notification.

3) Exceptional holds and legal requests
- Legal hold: We support legal hold requests and will pause the normal deletion lifecycle for affected records. Legal hold requires an authorized request from the customer (or subpoena/valid court order).
- Incident forensics: For security incidents we may retain a targeted set of artifacts up to 1 year, but only the minimal subset necessary for investigation. Customers are notified if their data is included.

4) Controls and evidence
- Access controls: All raw payloads and snapshots are encrypted at rest and require role-based access; access logs are retained separately.
- Export and deletion: Customers can request export of their data and immediate deletion; deletion operation returns a confirmation token.
- Attestation: We can produce a short attestation PDF confirming the no-training commitment and retention windows for procurement (I will attach SOC2 summary and a diagram).

Attachments: redwood-data-flow-diagram.png (visual overview), SOC2_summary.pdf (high-level controls)

Let me know if you want narrower TTLs for the pilot — we can lock to 7/30/90 or shorter per contract.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
